facts.text: Cayuga was named in 1894 by postmaster William Alonzo Davenport after his hometown of Cayuga, New York.
The first Methodist Church in northwestern Anderson County was built by settlers in Cayuga, followed by a Judson Baptist Church in a brush arbor and an early cemetery now called Old Judson Cemetery.
Cayuga grew in the 1880s from earlier settlements—Gilmore’s Chapel, Wild Cat Bluff, and Bethel—established in the late 1840s and early 1850s.
Oil struck Cayuga in 1934 when the Tidewater Oil Company discovered a new field, turning the quiet farming community into an overnight boomtown.
By 1936 Cayuga’s population swelled to over 1,000 residents and 15 businesses, but the boom faded and the town returned to a modest 56 people by 1974.
Cayuga sits at the junction of U.S. 79 and Farm‑to‑Market Road 114, a crossroads that helped shape its early development.
